correctness.rationale: Shared edge-clock survival and inclusion–exclusion give exact mixed falling-factorial moments and the finite joint completion law. Conditioning on the unique edge which completes its row and column yields an exact synchronized-arrival subprobability density and, after finite integration, a rational formula for every pair of part sizes at least two. At finite critical imbalance, the mixed factorial moments yield independent Poisson and Gumbel limits. Explicit domination of the rescaled tie density, obtained from independent disjoint-edge rows or columns in the residual graph, allows dominated convergence and gives the inverse-linear coincidence probability with a sharp hyperbolic-cosine coefficient. A change of variables proves a conditional gamma distribution with shape two. Exact finite independent checks covered all edge rankings through three-by-three, two-time edge-history counts, and a complete two-row special-family identity; 51 assertions passed. Infinite limits are proved mathematically, not claimed from enumeration.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns a synchronized last isolated-row/column disappearance in a distinct-edge bipartite graph process, including an exact finite probability, its leading critical-imbalance rare-event coefficient, and a conditional shape-two gamma law. Published first-order isolated-count results, repeated-draw coverage work and same-edge-order forest component counts examined do not state or directly imply these finer probability-level claims. Historical coupon-collection generating-function coverage remains a priority risk, and the comparison is not a universal novelty certificate.
residual_risks: The full Saltykov 1995 paper was not inspected; a general joint-distribution identity could cover the new rare tie event implicitly.
Historical two-type coupon collection or random-matrix occupancy literature may contain an equivalent coefficient or conditional timing law without matching contemporary terminology.
No independent expert audit or certification of originality has been performed.

The same-process Markov recurrence in Berikkyzy et al. may permit elementary extraction of the finite synchronized finish probability; the claimed contribution includes the sharp imbalance scaling and conditional time law beyond that recurrence.

value.rationale: The synchronized last-isolation event is a natural obstruction-clearing event in the same random bipartite growth model for which isolated vertices govern sparse thresholds. It is invisible to first-order independent Poisson and Gumbel approximations because its probability vanishes at the inverse-linear scale. The exact all-parameter finite formula, calibrated coefficient, and conditional hitting-time law reveal genuinely finer structure. The critical logarithmic part-size imbalance describes a natural competition window and shows how rare coincidence depends on the probabilities of winning on either side. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerically isolated calculation.
